confirmed: time_series accepts start_date and end_date in the formats 2006-01-02 and 2006-01-02T15:04:05. Source: https://twelvedata.com/docs/llms/market-data/time-series.md. The live copy is byte-identical to the earlier agent's saved copy. Both of my demo calls returned exactly the requested range.
Both bounds are inclusive for intraday (1min). Four calls agree: the earlier agent's call1 and call2, plus my fc1 (first bar 11:58, last 10:00) and fc2 (first 20:50, last 23:00).

When a range holds more bars than outputsize, the newest N bars up to end_date are kept and the oldest dropped. Evidence: the earlier call2 and support article 5656039 ('end_date defines the maximum possible datetime value... The number of rows is entirely determined by the outputsize parameter'). The same article's start_date-only example returns 'the most recent 5 records', so paging backward with end_date is the correct method.

outputsize accepts 1 to 5000. It defaults to 30 when no dates are given and to the maximum when dates are given. Sources: the docs and the support article ('the maximum value to be set is 5000'). My fc1 had no outputsize and returned 4,203 bars.

time_series costs 1 credit per symbol per request. Credits reset each minute, and there are 'no hidden extra data weights unless explicitly stated' (https://twelvedata.com/pricing). The FAQ says a standard request costs 1 credit.

Basic is 8 credits/min and 800 per day, with the daily quota resetting 'at midnight UTC (00:00:00)'. 'paid plans have no daily limits'. Each request returns api-credits-used and api-credits-left headers. Source: https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5615854-credits. 'Adding these two values provides the total credit limit' (support article 5713553). Neither header appears on demo responses: absent on all 4 earlier calls and on my 2.

Every tier's credits and price match the plan JSON embedded in the pricing pages:
- Grow: 55/144/377 credits at $29/$49/$79 ($24/$41/$66 annual).
- Pro: 610/987/1597 at $99/$149/$229 ($82/$124/$191).
- Ultra: 2584/4181/10946 at $329/$499/$999 ($274/$416/$832).
- Venture: 610/1597/2584 at $149/$299/$499 ($124/$248/$414).
- Enterprise: $1,099 ($916 annual), 10,946 API credits, configurable up to 100,000 (pricing-page-config: minEnterpriseApiCredits 10946, max 100000).
- Markets: 3/27/76/85; Venture 76.
- SLA: Venture 99.95%, Enterprise 99.99%.
- A 12-month startup discount is offered.

The licensing quotes are verbatim.
- Individual plans: 'personal, internal, and non-commercial purposes'.
- Business plans: 'commercial, external, and professional use'.
- Basic: 'Internal non-display usage'. Grow: 'Internal display data access'. Ultra: 'Internal non-display data access'.
- Venture: 'External display data access', 'ideal for companies showcasing data on client-facing apps or websites'.
- Enterprise: 'External distribution market data'.
- Terms ('Last updated: January 1, 2026'): the Internal Use definition and sections 2.1, 2.2(e), 2.3(g), 2.3(l), 2.4, 5.6(b), 16.1(a) and 16.2(a) exist as quoted.

api_usage costs 1 credit. Fields: current_usage, plan_limit, and plan_category (docs example value 'enterprise'). daily_usage and plan_daily_limit are 'Returned only when the plan has a daily limit'. The docs mark the 'Authorization: apikey <key>' header as recommended. symbol_search has a show_plan parameter that returns access.plan and access.plan_business (OpenAPI SymbolSearchResponseItemAccess).

Exchange pages:
- Forex is 'Basic+', with daily data from Jan 1, 1980, intraday from Sep 20, 2019, and trial symbol EUR/USD.
- Commodity is 'Grow+'/'Venture+', with intraday from Jan 9, 2020, and trial symbol XAU/USD.
- The xau-usd page says '/time_series data via our API — starting from the Basic plan and above'.
- The EUR/USD 1min earliest_timestamp is 2020-04-07 06:54 UTC (unix 1586242440).

Which plan the project uses is UNDETERMINED. That conclusion holds.
- My own search finds Twelve Data only at supabase/functions/get-candles/index.ts:5,150-151,220,227,241 and src/pages/backtest.astro:358,380,405.
- .env.example:1-11 and wrangler.toml:1-9 have no Twelve Data key. PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md:290 is generic. supabase/config.toml does not exist.
- The DB snapshot all_public_tables.json lists 23 tables, none of them for candles.
- In git 238e42e, supabase/get-candles/index.ts:13 maps '15m', :35 reads TWELVE_DATA_KEY, :44 uses outputsize=300, and :49 has the 'limit aşımı' comment.

All code citations are accurate.
- index.ts:7: RATE_LIMIT_MAX=30, keyed per user+IP (:60), held in a per-isolate Map (:33).
- :216-217: outputsize clamped to 10-500.
- :220: apikey sent in the query string, with no timezone or date parameters.
- :226-235: a non-OK upstream response returns {error:'Data service unavailable', status} without reading the body.
- :240-261: the status==='error' branch, which maps 401/403 to 503.
- :264-291: the response is rebuilt with the function's own X-RateLimit headers.
- backtest.astro:234 sends '15m', which INTERVAL_MAP (:20-30) lacks, so it falls back to 1day (:210-213).
- :29: '1m' maps to '1month'.
- backtest.astro:394 parses with new Date(); :385-388 and :653 surface the generic error.

Forex bars have no volume field. Meta has currency_base, currency_quote and type 'Physical Currency', with no exchange_timezone. OHLC values come as strings. JSON is about 103 bytes per bar (fc1: 431,120 B / 4,203 bars).

The error body is {code, message, status:'error'}. HTTP 401 was measured for demo-key gating. The OpenAPI spec declares 400/401/403/404/414/429/500 responses for /time_series, so the claim of 'real HTTP status' is plausible, though only 401 was measured. The 429 example message is quoted correctly.

The licensing conclusion is a fair reading. Individual tiers and Basic do not cover showing candles to a commercial app's users. Venture is the minimum listed tier with external display. Written confirmation from sales is advisable because Terms 2.2(e) ties external display to 'a Redistribution Rights Add-On or separate written agreement'.

refuted.claim: 'A forex week is about 7,200 M1 bars, or about 374k per year', and the sizing built on it: about 75 calls per symbol per year, about 2.4M bars since April 2020, about 490 calls per symbol, about 3,900 calls for 8 symbols, about 5 Basic days, about 71 min on Grow-55 and about 6.5 min on Venture-610.
refuted.evidence:
Twelve Data's EUR/USD feed runs 24/7, weekends included.

Official source: https://twelvedata.com/exchanges/physical_currency says 'Trading hours 24/7' and 'Main market 00:00 - 23:59'. https://twelvedata.com/exchanges/commodity says the same.

My demo call fc2: GET https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series?symbol=EUR/USD&interval=1min&start_date=2026-10-09T20:50:00&end_date=2026-10-11T23:00:00&timezone=UTC&order=asc&apikey=demo, HTTP 200.
- 3,010 bars, with only 1 minute missing.
- Saturday 2026-10-10: 1,440 of 1,440 bars. The day's range is 62.6 pips (1.11891-1.12517), with an average 1-minute range of 1.02 pips, so these are not flat bars.
- Sunday 00:00-21:00 UTC: 1,260 of 1,260 bars.

Cross-checks:
- Aggregated to H1, fc2 matches agents2/td/eurusd_1h_wkend.json exactly in 50 of 50 hours.
- agents2/td/eurusd_1min_sat.json has 1,434 bars for Saturday 2026-01-17.

Corrected sizing:
- A week has about 10,080 bars and a year about 525,600, which is about 105 calls per symbol per year at 5,000 bars per call.
- From 2020-04-07 to now there are up to about 3.43M bars, or about 687 calls per symbol and about 5,500 calls for 8 symbols.
- That is about 6.9 days of Basic's daily quota, about 100 min on Grow-55 and about 9 min on Venture-610.
- This is an upper bound: weekend coverage before 2026 was not measured.

refuted.claim: start_date and end_date default to UTC for forex ('Default location: Forex and Cryptocurrencies - UTC'). The report repeats this from the docs, and its 'timezone/Exchange' facts never say what 'Exchange' means for forex.
refuted.evidence:
The 'Exchange' timezone for Forex and Commodity is Australia/Sydney. The exchange pages state 'Timezone Australia/Sydney' and 'All times are displayed in the Australia/Sydney timezone (AEDT, UTC+11:00)'. The report cited these pages but left this line out; the earlier agent's own saved web_pages/exch_physical_currency.txt contains 'Australia/Sydney' twice.

My demo call fc1 sent no timezone: GET https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series?symbol=EUR/USD&interval=1min&start_date=2026-10-14T11:58:00&end_date=2026-10-17T10:00:00&order=asc&apikey=demo, HTTP 200, 4,203 bars.
- The returned labels run exactly 11:58 to 10:00.
- All 121 bars of the UTC baseline (agents2/api_demo/call1.json, timezone=UTC, 10:00-12:00) appear in fc1 at exactly +11:00 (121 of 121 exact OHLC matches).
- So without timezone, both the output labels and the date filter use Sydney time, not UTC.
- agents2/td/eurusd_earliest_1min.json shows 16:54 for unix 1586242440 (06:54 UTC). That is +10 in April 2020 (AEST), which fits Sydney's DST.

The docs also say datetime is 'at local exchange time'. The report's quote dropped those words.

refuted.claim: 'start_date and end_date are both inclusive' and 'A date-only end_date means 00:00:00 of that day, and that bar is included', stated as general rules.
refuted.evidence:
These were measured only on 1min bars with timezone=UTC.

The official support article https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5656039-how-to-get-historical-prices gives end_date=2020-05-06 on AAPL 1day. It returns [2020-05-05, 2020-05-04, 2020-05-01, 2020-04-30, 2020-04-29]. 2020-05-06 was a Wednesday trading day, yet it is excluded.

So inclusivity is not established for daily intervals. Without timezone, '00:00' means Sydney midnight, which is 13:00 UTC the previous day under AEDT.

issues.issue: Twelve Data forex data includes weekend bars, so replay would show them. Saturday bars carry real ranges (62.6 pips on 2026-10-10). cTrader charts, which this app syncs, have none. A replay would therefore show candles, and could fill SL/TP, at times a broker cannot trade. All the report's quota and storage estimates are about 40% too low (10,080 vs 7,200 bars a week). The commodity page also says 24/7; XAU/USD weekends are unmeasured because the demo key refuses gold.
issues.fix: Store raw M1 bars as received, but give replay and aggregation an explicit session calendar. For example, exclude Friday 17:00 to Sunday 17:00 America/New_York, DST-aware, as a per-symbol setting the owner approves. Recompute sizing at 1,440 bars per day. Fetch history lazily on Basic. A full M1 prefetch for 8 symbols is up to about 27.5M rows, so check it against the Supabase plan's database size quota before choosing eager caching.

issues.issue: With timezone omitted, Twelve Data returns forex and commodity bars labelled in Australia/Sydney time and also reads start_date/end_date as Sydney time. The meta has no exchange_timezone to warn the client. The current production function omits timezone (supabase/functions/get-candles/index.ts:220), and src/pages/backtest.astro:394 parses the labels as browser-local time. For a UTC+3 user, every intraday forex or gold candle is therefore placed 8 h off (AEDT) or 7 h off (AEST). The offset also changes twice a year. At Sydney's April fall-back, labels 02:00-02:59 repeat. That hour falls on Saturday around 16:00 UTC, which has bars, so the series gets duplicate timestamps. Those duplicates would break the chart's ascending-time order and collide with any cache keyed by label.
issues.fix: Always send timezone=UTC, with UTC start_date/end_date in the 2006-01-02T15:04:05 form. Parse the result as UTC: append 'Z', or use Date.UTC. Store timestamptz keyed on (symbol, interval, ts). Add a contract test that the first returned bar equals start_date when timezone=UTC.

issues.issue: Twelve Data's 1day forex bars do not start at UTC midnight. In October 2026 a bar runs 20:00 to 20:00 UTC, which is 07:00 Sydney or 16:00 New York. I derived this by matching agents2/td/eurusd_1day.json bars 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16 against all four OHLC values of my own M1 data (fc1) over 20:00-UTC windows; no other window matched all four. The docs say the timezone parameter is ignored for 1day/1week/1month. These bars therefore match neither broker D1 candles (17:00 New York) nor UTC days, and the boundary moves with DST.
issues.fix: Do not cache or display Twelve Data 1day/1week bars as forex D1/W1. Build every higher timeframe from UTC M1 with an explicit 17:00 New York boundary, which the report already recommends for intraday. Note in the plan that native daily bars are off-boundary.

issues.issue: The report generalizes bound inclusivity from 1min tests to all intervals. Official docs contradict it for daily intervals. Cache-coverage bookkeeping that relies on inclusive bounds can leave gaps or duplicates.
issues.fix: Make ingestion independent of bound semantics. Request [start, end] in UTC and upsert with ON CONFLICT (symbol, interval, ts) DO NOTHING. Mark a day covered only after counting the rows, or after the response's last bar reaches the window end. Page backward by setting end_date to the oldest bar minus 1 interval.

issues.issue: The claim that 'errors come back with the matching HTTP status' rests on a single measured status: the demo-key 401. Other 4xx codes, and 429 in particular, are supported only by the docs (the OpenAPI per-status responses and the errors table).
issues.fix: In the new function, read and parse the JSON body for every upstream response, OK or not. Handle both a non-2xx status and body.status==='error'. Log code, message and the api-credits-used/left headers on the server only, and return a sanitized error to the browser.

issues.issue: The secret name changed. The initial commit 238e42e read TWELVE_DATA_KEY (supabase/get-candles/index.ts:35); the current code reads TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY (supabase/functions/get-candles/index.ts:5). If the secret was never renamed, the live function returns 503 'Service not configured', and the question of which plan the key is on cannot be settled until the right key is found.
issues.fix: Before running the api_usage check, the owner should open the Supabase dashboard's Edge Function secrets page (it shows names only) and confirm that TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY exists. This is the owner's own read-only action on production; nothing should be changed without approval.

issues.issue: backtest.astro:394 parses dates with new Date(). Date-only strings ('YYYY-MM-DD', returned for 1day) are parsed as UTC under ECMAScript. 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' is implementation-defined: Chromium and Firefox treat it as local time, and older Safari returns Invalid Date. The same page therefore handles daily and intraday bars differently.
issues.fix: Request timezone=UTC and convert explicitly, for example Date.parse(s.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'), or return epoch seconds from the Edge Function.

report:
FACT-CHECK: TWELVE DATA REPORT (2026-10-18)

The report's main conclusions hold: date ranges are supported, the plan cannot be determined, and Venture is the licensing minimum. Three things need fixing: the sizing number, the timezone behaviour, and the claim about daily bounds.

METHOD
- I re-fetched the official sources:
  - Three docs pages: time-series.md, api-usage.md and introduction.md. All three are byte-identical to the earlier agent's saved copies.
  - The individual and business pricing pages. The per-tier quota and price JSON is embedded in the HTML.
  - The terms page, three support articles, and the forex, commodity and XAU/USD pages.
- I re-checked every repo citation and searched the repo and git history myself.
- I made exactly 2 demo-key calls. I did not contact Supabase or any Edge Function. The repo is untouched (git status clean). Scratch files are under agents2\factcheck.

WHAT HOLDS UP
- **Date ranges are supported.** start_date and end_date work in both formats. Intraday bounds are inclusive. When a range holds more bars than outputsize, the newest N are kept; the support article backs this.
- **Parameters and cost.** outputsize runs 1 to 5000 and defaults to the maximum when dates are given. The cost is 1 credit per symbol, with the quota reset every minute.
- **Plans.** Basic is 8/min and 800/day, reset at 00:00 UTC. Every Grow, Pro, Ultra, Venture and Enterprise tier and price matches the embedded pricing JSON exactly.
- **Licensing.** All quotes are verbatim. Venture is the lowest listed tier with 'External display data access'. Terms 2.2(e) still makes written confirmation from sales prudent.
- **Plan checks.** api_usage, symbol_search show_plan and the advice on how to map plans to tiers are all accurate.
- **Which plan we use.** It cannot be determined from the repo, git history or DB snapshots. My search found Twelve Data only in get-candles/index.ts and backtest.astro.
- **Code findings.** All of them are correct:
  - '15m' falls back to 1day.
  - '1m' maps to 1month.
  - The key is sent in the query string.
  - Non-2xx response bodies are discarded.
  - The rate limiter is per isolate.

WHAT IS WRONG OR MISSING
1. **Forex runs 24/7.** The exchange page says 'Trading hours 24/7'. My call fc2 (UTC, Friday 20:50 to Sunday 23:00) returned all 1,440 bars for Saturday, with a 62.6-pip range, and all 1,260 Sunday bars up to 21:00 UTC. The '7,200 bars per week / 374k per year' basis is wrong. The real figures are about 10,080 per week and 525,600 per year, so every quota estimate rises by about 40%. The replay also has to decide whether to hide weekend bars, because cTrader charts have none.
2. **The default timezone for forex and gold is Australia/Sydney.** The official exchange pages say so; the report cited those pages but left that line out. My call fc1 sent no timezone and came back labelled exactly 11 hours ahead of UTC (121 of 121 bars matched). The start and end filters were also read in Sydney time, despite the docs saying 'Forex - UTC'. The response meta does not include the timezone.
   - Production impact: get-candles sends no timezone and the page parses dates as local time. For users at UTC+3, intraday forex candles are therefore shifted by 8 hours (7 hours from April to October). Sydney's clock change in April also creates a repeated hour of timestamps.
3. **Inclusive bounds are proven only for intraday bars.** The official support example for daily AAPL bars leaves out the end date.
4. **Daily forex bars run 20:00 to 20:00 UTC** in October 2026 (07:00 Sydney time). The timezone setting is ignored for daily bars. Build daily and weekly candles from UTC minute bars instead.
5. **Error status codes.** Twelve Data returning the real HTTP status was measured only for the demo-key 401. For other codes it rests on the docs. The new code should read the response body in every case.
6. **Secret name.** The first version of the function read TWELVE_DATA_KEY; the current code reads TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY. The owner should confirm the secret exists under the new name before running the plan check.

A NOTE ON THE EARLIER EVIDENCE
The earlier agent's folder agents2\td holds 12 more demo responses that the report never mentions, with Date headers between 15:35 and 15:41 UTC. They may come from a parallel agent. They already showed the weekend bars and the Sydney offset, and they match my own measurements exactly (50 of 50 hourly bars; two daily bars matched on open, high, low and close).

EVIDENCE FILES

  - fc1 (15:57:22 UTC): EUR/USD 1min, 2026-10-14T11:58:00 to 2026-10-17T10:00:00, no timezone.
  - fc2 (16:00:50 UTC): EUR/USD 1min, 2026-10-09T20:50:00 to 2026-10-11T23:00:00, timezone=UTC.
